claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you some questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

Since Alex is 17 years old, the key factor is whether he's still in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This could include things like A-levels, college courses, certain vocational training, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he has, and it's been within the last 20 weeks since he left education, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit during that period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with careers services or the armed forces. He just finished school and is taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**When did Alex finish school or leave education?** (I need to know if it was recent or some time ago)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished school a few months ago, back in the summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Does Alex currently work in paid employment for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more question:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me also confirm a couple of final details:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**
2. **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, and yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Since Alex is 17 years old and has left education, Child Benefit would normally continue only if he remains in approved education or training. However, Alex is not currently in any approved education or training.

There is an alternative provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education - **but only if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services**. Since Alex hasn't registered with either of these, this extension doesn't apply.

**What could make Alex eligible again:**
- If Alex returns to approved education or training (like college, A-levels, or certain vocational courses)
- If he registers with a careers service now, you might be able to claim for up to 20 weeks from when he left education (though this may depend on timing)

If Alex does decide to pursue education, training, or register with careers services, you should contact HMRC to update your circumstances, as this could restore your eligibility.
